benchmark_question: Does slop-test-detector make the model better at reviewing test files for weak tests than baseline?

evals.name: empty-and-commented
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
evals.expected_output: Detects empty_test_body and commented_out_assertions as must-fail, plus no_production_call
expectations: Identifies 'empty_test_body' on 'should process refund for valid transaction'
Identifies 'empty_test_body' on 'should validate card number format before charging'
Identifies 'commented_out_assertions' on 'should validate card number format before charging'
Classifies empty_test_body as must-fail severity
Classifies commented_out_assertions as must-fail severity
Identifies 'no_production_call' on 'should log transaction with correlation ID'
Does NOT flag 'should reject expired cards' — it has proper assertions and throws
Explains that empty test bodies pass regardless of behavior
Provides line numbers for each finding

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should reject expired cards

evals.name: tautological-circus
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
evals.expected_output: Detects tautological_assertion, conditional_assertion, truthiness_only, and no_production_call
expectations: Identifies 'tautological_assertion' on 'should hash password with bcrypt rounds' (assert.ok(true))
Identifies 'tautological_assertion' on 'should match known hash to original plaintext' (identical literals)
Identifies 'conditional_assertion' on 'should enforce rate limit after 5 failed attempts'
Classifies tautological_assertion as must-fail severity
Classifies conditional_assertion as must-fail severity
Identifies 'truthiness_only' on 'should hash password with bcrypt rounds'
Does NOT flag 'should generate valid JWT with correct claims' — it has proper value assertions
Explains that assert.ok(true) always passes and verifies nothing
Explains that conditional assertions may execute zero assertions

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should generate valid JWT with correct claims

evals.name: truthiness-and-type-only
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
expectations: Identifies 'assert_on_type_not_value' on 'should detect column types from sample data'
Identifies 'truthiness_only' on 'should generate report ID for pipeline run'
Identifies 'assert_return_type_only' on 'should generate report ID for pipeline run'
Does NOT flag 'should aggregate numeric columns with correct totals' — it asserts actual values
Explains that typeof-only assertions verify shape but not actual behavior
Explains that assert.ok(identifier) only checks existence, not correctness
Provides line numbers for each finding

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should aggregate numeric columns with correct totals

evals.name: roundtrip-schema
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
evals.expected_output: Detects literal_roundtrip, schema_success_only, duplicate_assertion_set, and no_production_call
expectations: Identifies 'literal_roundtrip' on 'should store display name from creation payload'
Identifies 'literal_roundtrip' on 'should preserve timezone setting'
Identifies 'schema_success_only' on 'should validate email format with schema'
Identifies 'schema_success_only' on 'should accept valid profile payload'
Identifies 'duplicate_assertion_set' on 'should accept valid profile payload'
Explains that literal roundtrip tests only verify serialization, not logic
Explains that checking only .success misses .data field and .error.issues validation
Does NOT report 'schema_success_only' on 'should reject profile with missing email' — that test checks .error.issues

evals.name: duplicate-no-variation
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
expectations: Identifies 'duplicate_assertion_set' on 'should shorten HTTPS URL to 8-char slug'
Identifies 'duplicate_assertion_set' on 'should classify URL protocol for redirect'
Identifies 'no_input_variation' on 'should classify URL protocol for redirect'
Explains that identical assertion sequences indicate copy-paste without differentiation
Explains that calling the same function with identical args provides no additional coverage
Does NOT flag 'should track click count per slug' — it has unique assertions and inputs

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should track click count per slug

Identifies 'no_production_call' on 'should handle nested keys with dot notation'

Explains that testing only happy paths misses error handling
Explains that tests without production function calls test language guarantees, not app code

evals.name: false-positive-helpers
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. The file uses custom assertion helpers (assertEventEmitted, assertPayloadContains, testDeliveryOrder) that internally call assert.*. Configure assertionEquivalents accordingly. Report all findings.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize assertion equivalents and NOT flag tests as empty or truthiness-only. May flag no_negative_test.
expectations: Does NOT flag 'empty_test_body' on any test — assertion equivalents are present
Does NOT flag 'truthiness_only' on any test — assertion equivalents count as real assertions
Recognizes assertEventEmitted, assertPayloadContains, testDeliveryOrder as assertion equivalents
If it reports any findings, they are limited to no_negative_test (legitimate: no throws/rejects)

evals.name: false-positive-conditional
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns. Use the slop-test-detector to analyze it. Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
evals.expected_output: No slop findings — conditional setup is different from conditional assertions, and commented code coexists with active assertions
expectations: Reports zero findings or states no slop was detected
Does NOT flag 'conditional_assertion' — assertions are AFTER the if block, not inside it
Does NOT flag 'commented_out_assertions' — active assertions exist alongside commented ones
Reports a score of 100 or states the file is clean

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should return default value
should evaluate flag based on user segment
should track evaluation metrics
should throw when flag configuration is invalid

Explains that fc.property with return true and no assertions passes vacuously
Explains that .length >= 0 is always true and cannot fail
Does NOT flag 'should rank exact matches higher than partial' — proper value assertions
Does NOT flag 'should handle empty query gracefully' — proper value assertion

evals.name: defect-comments
evals.prompt: Review this test file for weak test patterns using the STRICT preset of slop-test-detector (all 18 rules enabled, including missing_defect_comment and trivial_defect_comment). Report all findings with rule names, line numbers, severity, and explain the impact of each issue.
evals.expected_output: Detects missing_defect_comment and trivial_defect_comment on tests without adequate Defect: comments
expectations: Identifies 'missing_defect_comment' on 'should evict least recently used entry when at capacity'
Identifies 'missing_defect_comment' on 'should respect max size limit'
Identifies 'trivial_defect_comment' on 'should handle TTL expiry correctly'
Does NOT flag 'should update access order on get to maintain LRU invariant' with missing or trivial defect — it has a proper Defect: comment
Explains that Defect: comments must describe what breaks, for whom, and the consequence
Explains that trivial defect comments (fewer than 10 words) don't convey enough information

forbidden_rules_on_clean_tests: should update access order on get to maintain LRU invariant
